column1: # UCSC db -> NCBI RefSeq accession: the OVERRIDE layer over the detection in
# src/deriveNcbiAccessions.ts, which is what downloadNcbiGff.sh actually reads.
# Columns: db <tab> accession <tab> assemblyName
#   db           UCSC golden-path / hub assembly name
#   accession    GCF_ RefSeq accession whose annotation to download,
#                or `-` to build no GFF for this db at all
#   assemblyName human-readable note only (not parsed)
# A row here wins over anything derived, so add one when detection is wrong or
# absent -- not to record an answer detection already gets right.
# Four of the rows below are load-bearing rather than redundant. hg38, hg19,
# mm39 and hs1 have no ucsc<->refseq row in hgFixed.asmEquivalent, and the only
# accession their genome-list entry names is the GenBank submission
# (GCA_000001405.15 for hg38), whose seqids a RefSeq GFF never uses. Detection
# finds nothing for them; delete these rows and the four assemblies people
# actually open lose their GFF. The rest (ce11, danRer11, dm6, mm10, rn6, rn7,
# sacCer3) are recovered by asmEquivalent and kept only because a curated pick
# beats a derived one when the two ever disagree.
# Policy: each accession is the latest RefSeq annotation on the SAME assembly as
# the UCSC db (not merely the same species), so the GFF's RefSeq seqids match the
# db's chromAlias. Picking by species alone is wrong: hg19 and hg38 are both
# GCA_000001405.*, mm10/mm39 both GCA_000001635.*, etc. -- only the assembly
# differs. The assembly's refNameAliases (UCSC chromAlias.txt) maps the GFF's
# RefSeq accession seqids (NC_000001.11) to UCSC names (chr1) at load time, so the
# GFF is used as-is with no seqid rewriting.
